title: Early Raeburn records, V-discs, Jubilee and pirate reissues
summary: Schremp lists the 1944 sessions and the Jubilee broadcast, and Handy objects to unauthorised reissues.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: The first release, as we go through this thing,--the first release, 1944, was "Starlight Avenue", "I Dream Of You", "This Must Be Love" and "It Could Happen To You".
Those are, I guess, pre-you.
Right. I don't even know if any of those are Fink's either.
As a matter of fact, you were on the band. I'm not aware of your writing any of those things.
No, I didn't.
The next was December 1944, was a series of V discs, and that date included "Two Spoos", "Tunesia," "Who Started Love," "Key F,"--
Key F?
K-E-Y, capital F. "Grey Suede," "Barefoot Boy With Cheek," which I think was "Barefoot Boyd With Cheek,"--
"Gray Suede?"
"Gray Suede." 1944.
I'd love to get a copy of that. I'm trying to find good copies of some of that stuff.
I've got a copy of "Gray Suede" on order.
In good condition?
A new one, there's a new pressing of it. It's that Jubilee.
Who's releasing that?
One of the pirates.
I think it's that Florida company.
How can you find out who the pirates are?
I'll tell you, I've got the name and address. I've got a catalog at home.
And these guys are re-leasing "Key F" and "Gray Suede?"
It's the same side with that Mel Torme and the Meltones interrupting the thing. You don't remember that date at all?
No.
It's a Jubilee radio program, I assume it was one of the wartime things, I've forgotten exactly how it worked. It had a

terribly noisy, loud, vulgar M.C. who invites you, he's going to play the new George Handy Symphony, symphonic jazz, and he invites you to the microphone to explain what is jazz or what is symphonic jazz, and then you play "Dalvatore" and whichever is second of the four. Then Torme does two tunes and then you play three and then the fourth one is, I guess, "Look Ma". I've forgotten which.
"Key F" was last.
There was something by Ella Mae Morse's little sister; do you remember the dialogue I'm talking about?
Yeah. A big black guy was the thing.*
That's the thing that's being released on these records.
That was the radio show, the armed forces radio show I think.
Hindsight is the name of the releasing company.
How the hell can they
*Emcee was actor Ernie Whitman.
release music of mine that they have no right to release.
I don't know; I can't answer that.
Well, people have been doing this for years. I can't imagine the money that's out there that belongs to me.

I'll get you copies of the record anyway. I've got one on order. It's very late. I've had it on order for six months--or six weeks, but when I get it I'll see that you get a clean copy, if nothing else.
Hindsight Records.

I think it's Hindsight. There are two or three companies like that. I think Hindsight is the one that has this. There's another company in Chicago and there's one out on the coast that does that sort of thing.
